Chapter Nine: The Ongoing Struggle—Justice, Imagination, and the Work Left to Do.
Even now, years after Harriet Tubman’s passing, the world she worked so hard to change is still a work in progress. The fight for justice is far from over. You can see it in courtrooms, hear it in classrooms, and feel it in those quiet, honest conversations with friends and neighbors.
The questions Harriet faced? They’re still with us today. Who truly gets to be free? Who do we choose to remember? And what does it really look like to imagine a better world?
There’s this moment that seems to repeat with every generation—a person stands at a crossroads, unsure of which direction to take. The way forward is hazy. The risks? They're real. But that glimmer of hope, that chance for change, is always there.
Harriet’s story gives us something special. It’s not a map of roads and rivers, but a map of courage and imagination. It reminds us that what’s possible is always shifting—that the work of justice never really ends.
Most of us don’t see ourselves as heroes. We just live our lives, do what needs doing, help out when we can. But if Harriet’s life teaches us anything, it’s that ordinary people, when faced with extraordinary moments, can change the world.
Think about the Underground Railroad. It wasn’t built by legends or saints. It came together because neighbors, friends, and even strangers decided to step up and make a difference.
At the heart of every movement for justice, you’ll find imagination. It’s that ability to look past what’s right in front of us, to believe that things can get better. Harriet’s life proves just how powerful imagination can be—not as a way to escape, but as a tool for survival, and for real transformation.
Sure, the work that’s left can feel overwhelming. Injustice still exists. Memories can fade. And sometimes, settling for less feels easier.
But here’s what matters: the stories we share, the choices we make, and the dreams we hold onto—they can keep hope alive.
Harriet’s legacy isn’t just a story from the past. It’s a call to action. It’s a reminder that our future is shaped by those who dare to imagine it.
